identity.title: Local Enhancement of the Surface Density in the Protoplanetary Ring Surrounding HD 142527
identity.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan

paper_type_evidence.quote: We report ALMA observations of dust continuum, $^{13}$CO $J=$ 3–2, and C$^{18}$O $J=$ 3–2 line emission toward a gapped protoplanetary disk around HD 142527.

evidence.quote: The distance is assumed to be 140 pc in this paper considering the association to Sco OB2.

distance_source.value: assumed from association to Sco OB2

evidence.quote: The distance is assumed to be 140 pc in this paper considering the association to Sco OB2.

question.value: What are the surface density and gravitational stability of the strongly asymmetric outer ring of HD 142527, using continuum and 13CO/C18O 3-2 data to constrain grain temperature?

evidence.quote: To evaluate the surface density in this region, the grain temperature needs to be constrained and was estimated from the optically thick $^{13}$CO $J =$ 3–2 emission.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00318.S.
HD 142527 was observed with ALMA in Band 7 using 20–26 12-m antennas in the Extended array configuration in Cycle 0.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 spectral windows, 469 MHz each, 3840 channels, 0.122 MHz (0.11 km/s) spacing; centers 330.588, 329.331, 342.883, 342.400 GHz

evidence.quote: The central frequencies for these windows are 330.588, 329.331, 342.883, and 342.400 GHz, respectively
allowing observations of molecular lines of $^{13}$CO $J=3$–2, C$^{18}$O $J=3$–2, and CS $J=7$–6.

the latter corresponded to the largest angular scale of the detectable component of $10\ensuremath{''}$.

sensitivity.value: continuum rms 0.19 mJy/beam; 13CO 12 and C18O 15 mJy/beam per 0.11 km/s channel

evidence.quote: The rms noise is 0.19 mJy beam$^{-1}$ for the continuum whereas it is 12 and 15 mJy beam$^{-1}$ in the 0.11 km s$^{-1}$ wide channels

observing_dates.value: June to August 2012, four scheduling blocks

evidence.quote: The observations reported in this letter consisted of four scheduling blocks over the period from June to August 2012.

an abundance ratio of X(C$^{13}$O)/X(C$^{18}$O) $\sim$ 7 (cite: qi11)

pipeline_or_manual.value: CASA flagging then bandpass, gain, flux scaling calibration; manual/pipeline not specified

evidence.quote: After flagging aberrant data and applying calibrations for the bandpass, gain, and flux scaling, the corrected visibilities were imaged
Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA) package, version 3.4.
The absolute flux density was determined from observations of Titan and Neptune.
The uncertainty associated with the absolute flux density is 10%.

self_calibration.value: Continuum self-cal: phase-only with six iterations, then one phase+amplitude; applied to 13CO and C18O

evidence.quote: The phase alone was corrected first via six iterative model refinements, then the calibration was obtained for phase-plus-amplitude with no iteration.
the corrected visibilities were imaged and deconvolved using the CLEAN algorithm with Briggs weighting with a robust parameter of 0.5.

weighting_robust.value: Briggs robust 0.5 initially; final CLEAN with Uniform weighting for continuum and lines

evidence.quote: The final CLEANing was performed with Uniform weighting both for the continuum and emission lines.

continuum_subtraction.value: underlying continuum subtracted from line data

evidence.quote: The line results above were obtained after subtracting the underlying continuum, which is the typical method adopted in earlier studies.
those for $^{13}$CO and C$^{18}$O are $0.43\ensuremath{''} \times 0.37\ensuremath{''}$ with PA = $50\ensuremath{^\circ}$.
The rms noise is 0.19 mJy beam$^{-1}$ for the continuum

what.value: Dust opacity relation kappa=0.1(nu/1e12 Hz)^beta, beta=1

evidence.quote: on the basis of the conventional relation $\kappa_{\nu}=0.1(\nu / 10^{12}$ Hz)$^{\beta}$ with $\beta = 1.0$ ((cite: bec90); V11)
The 1+1D modeling (cite: nom09) was performed assuming the surface density estimated as above

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate, self-calibrate and image continuum and lines

method.value: CASA calibration, CLEAN imaging, continuum self-cal applied to lines

evidence.quote: The solution for the continuum was applied to $^{13}$CO and C$^{18}$O data.
The final CLEANing was performed with Uniform weighting both for the continuum and emission lines.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit Keplerian rotation to 13CO to get inclination and systemic velocity

method.value: Gaussian peak velocity along major axis every 0.03", then S/N-weighted least-squares Keplerian fit

evidence.quote: S/N-weighted least-squares fitting of an analytic Keplerian equation was performed to the measured peak velocity as a function of radius.

key_parameters.value: free: systemic velocity, center, inclination; stellar mass fixed at 2.2±0.3 Msun

evidence.quote: the systemic velocity, position of the center of mass (the star), and inclination relative to an observer are set as free parameters

evidence.loc: Results, Integrated Intensity and Gas Kinematics
evidence.quote: Then, S/N-weighted least-squares fitting of an analytic Keplerian equation was performed to the measured peak velocity as a function of radius.

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate grain temperature from optically thick 13CO brightness temperature

method.value: Add continuum Tb to line peak Tb after beam matching; take 13CO Tb at continuum peak (36 K) as upper bound on dust temperature

evidence.quote: we conservatively regard 36 K, which is the $T_b$($^{13}$CO) at the radius of continuum peak, as an upper bound of the grain temperature
we assume the same excitation temperature ($T_{\rm ex}$) for both lines and an abundance ratio of X(C$^{13}$O)/X(C$^{18}$O) $\sim$ 7

analysis_steps.goal: Derive dust optical depth and surface density lower limit

method.value: Compare Tdust with continuum Tb to get tau, convert with kappa_336=0.034 cm2/g for g/d=100

evidence.quote: using $\tau = 0.9$ along with $\kappa_{336} = 0.034$ cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ for a g/d of 100
Assuming a g/d of 100 and a temperature of 36 K, the fitted Gaussian to the azimuthally-averaged one has a peak surface density

validation.value: 1+1D vertical radiative transfer reproduced observed Tb

evidence.quote: The observed $T_b$ was reproduced when using a grain opacity plausible for protoplanetary disks (cite: nom05).

analysis_steps.goal: Radial Gaussian fit and Toomre Q

method.value: Gaussian fit to deprojected radial profile per PA and azimuthal average; compute Toomre Q with isothermal sound speed at 36 K, M*=2.2 Msun

evidence.quote: resulting in $Q(R = 161~{\rm{AU}}) = 2.2$ using $\Sigma_{\rm{average}} = 11$ g cm$^{-2}$, the isothermal sound speed for 36 K, and a stellar mass of $2.2~M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$.
the Toomre’s $Q$ parameter (cite: too64) was computed under the assumption of a g/d of 100.
The data were calibrated and analyzed using the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA) package, version 3.4.
The contrast in flux density thus reaches to 30 between the northern peak and the SW minimum.

results_numeric.quantity: Outer disk total flux density at 336 GHz

evidence.quote: the total flux density ($>5\sigma$) was measured as 2.7 Jy
The peak flux density is expressed by a brightness temperature ($T_b$) of 24 K
The integrated flux density over the Gaussian was 2.3$\pm$0.2 mJy
the inclination was estimated as $i = 26.9^{+2.2}_{-1.8}$ degrees
The systemic velocity was determined as $3.70 \pm 0.02$ km s$^{-1}$.
the surface density was calculated as $\Sigma_{\rm peak}=$ 28.1 g cm$^{-2}$
Integrating the surface density yielded a mass for the entire outer disk of 0.09 $M_{\odot}$
Locally estimated at the horseshoe peak at $R = 156$ AU, $Q$ was obtained as 0.9 for $\Sigma_{\rm peak} = 28$ g cm$^{-2}$.
the total (gas and dust) disk mass was then calculated as $(4.3 \pm 0.4) \times 10^{-5}~M_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$

findings_qualitative.value: Gas velocity field is consistent with simple circular Keplerian rotation; dust streamers reported earlier were not confirmed.

evidence.quote: Dust streamers from the outer disk reported in the previous study (cite: cas13) were not confirmed.

claims.hypothesis: Is the northern horseshoe locally very dense?
claims.experiment: Estimate Tdust from 13CO Tb, derive tau and Sigma
claims.finding: Region is locally massive and may be gravitationally unstable (Q<~1-2)

evidence.quote: The lower limit of the peak surface density was then calculated to be 28 g cm$^{-2}$ by assuming a canonical gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100.

claims.hypothesis: Can the asymmetry be due to eccentric dust orbits?
claims.experiment: Gaussian fits to radial profile at each PA
claims.result: Anticorrelation between peak intensity and deprojected distance

evidence.quote: The anti-correlation excludes the possible explanation that the azimuthal asymmetry is due to eccentric orbits of the dust particles.

claims.hypothesis: Could the ring be stable if gas is depleted?
claims.experiment: Consider lower g/d with C18O optical depth
claims.finding: Alternatively dust accumulation, possible rocky core formation

evidence.quote: In this case, lower gas-to-dust ratio by at least 1 order of magnitude is required, implying possible formation of a rocky planetary core.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Eccentric dust orbits rejected as cause of asymmetry

evidence.quote: The anti-correlation excludes the possible explanation that the azimuthal asymmetry is due to eccentric orbits of the dust particles.

limitations_admitted.value: Q is an upper limit and g/d assumption is a caveat; optical thickness of C18O uncertain, so derived g/d is a limit

evidence.quote: The caveat in the above discussion is the assumption of the g/d

referee_caveats_inferred: Dust temperature set to upper bound from 13CO surface Tb; midplane could be colder or warmer
Single opacity law assumed; grain growth would change Sigma
Low inclination makes kinematic constraints weak
No formal fitting uncertainties on surface density
